composers.name: Andres Bosshard
composers.bioText: 1955, lives and works in Zürich, Köln, Berlin, Wien, 1996 to 2001 collaborations with IGNCA in New Delhi. Andres Bosshard is an extraordinarily versatile artist who began as a painter but soon expanded into actions and performances before turning to experimental music theatre. He has developed solar powered sound-objects, interactive computer music programs and multichannel sound installations. His most important projects: " Dam in Fusio" (1987), " Sound Bridge Bern" (1990), " telefonia" (1991) a simultaneous satellite-link concert (sound and video streamng between New York and Winterthur. Bosshard was co-author and responsible for the sound mixing of te collective projects "chip radio" (ORF radio 1992); "realtime" (ORF radio and TV, 1993); "manandarbandr" sonambiente, Berlin (1996); media-architecture for the"Klangturm" in St.Pölten, Austria (1995-98); Fellow at the khm (academy of media arts Cologne) (1997/8), expo project "Wasserspuren" for Hann.Münden (2000); expo project "Klangallee" Bad Pyrmont (2000). Expo project"Agora", a sound land art theatre in the shape of a giant ear, Nitterfeld (Leipzig) (since 2000) Artistic director of the sound tower in Biel for the National expo02 in Switzerland (2002). He was part of “Radiotopia”, Ars Electronica, Linz 2002. First presentation of the"rotobossophon", Dresden November 2002. Rotophonia, Singuhr Hoergallerie Parochial Kirche, Berlin 2003 Guest Professor at the khm (academy of media arts Cologne) 2003. 1. composers.name: Dino Bramanti
composers.bioText: Dino Bramanti was born in 1969 in Pietrasanta (Lucca), Italy. His background is based on a classical humanistic education and on mathematical and technical studies. In 1996 took PhD in Telecommunications Engineering at the University of Pisa in Italy, achieving a strong training in digital signal processing, computer science and communications networks and protocols. During 90's he's been working as DJ in several clubs and radio stations in the area of black music, 60's funk and dub and started moving towards electronic sound composition, digital signal manipulation and sample grinding. In 2002 designs and builds, with the collaboration of A. Borghi, "quaa|ude - a quiet interlude" installation working as natural sound generator and real-time processor, which has been premiered in October 2002 at "c'Arte d'identita' " art gallery in Pietrasanta (LU). As a Timet collaborator of has taken part in several projects contributing with concepts, sound composition, audio and electronics engineering. He's collaborated to Timet's Compilatione project with a handful of sonic pills aimed at desecrating both dance stereotypes and classical-contemporary music forms. Latest involvement with Timet has been with "L'Ospite Ingrato - A Medici Obsession" sound installation in Florence, part of "ORIZZONTI- Belvedere dell' Arte" Art Exibition directed by A. Bonito Oliva (2003-04). He is currently working on the solo project ampang, based on real-time sound composition from custom designed software for rhythmic, dub-influenced structures and lines and he's carrying on bonarosa project, for laptop based live improvisation, with fellow A. Borghi. He' s sharing his time between digital art works and the work as network software designer for telecommunications industry. All his works are realized in MaxMSP, superCollider and Csound development environment. AMPANG ampang takes its move from the multitude of sounds which, actively or passively populate our daylife. They are sounds and noises captured in every time and place, voices fragments and clutter, short excerpts from crucial recordings and works. The only thing in common among them is that they are short. Sound events lasting about a second, such that their atomicity ensures that they are no more related to the original context. Those absolute sound snippets are the timbral starting point for the composition. A software application, designed and built for their continous processing, shapes them in real time over rythmic structures. It organizes them over time, in a semi-deterministic way, following the conceptual and operational add/drop approach mutuated from dub techniques. dino.bramanti@tiscali.it 1. lownext [ listen ] 3'53'' 2. trasto [ listen ] 4'54'' <home <back to guests // Last update:: October 30, 2013 //

composers.name: Davide Tidoni
composers.bioText: Davide Tidoni (Brescia, 1981). While studying drums, he realized that the instrument wasn't made just to keep the beat; the beat should be kept in one's head anyway. Davide loves it when amplifiers fizzle-out and break in an orgy of noise, or when old crazies speak to him. He unfortunatly hates most of the other things one sees in an average day. Playing mostly by himself, he has produced works for prepared drums, objects and electroacoustic music. The two tracks you can listen to are taken from “Hardgore”, a work for prepared drumset and electronics (2003) 1. primo contatto [ listen ] 3'42'' 1. taià le gambe col podèt [ listen ] 2'33'' <home <back to guests // Last update:: October 30, 2013 //

composers.name: Frank Schulte
composers.bioText: German sound creator Frank Schulte has played in various ensembles for improvised and composed sound art. He works with performance artists, dancer, actors and lyricists. He also composes music for plays, experiments with the application of new electronic sound generation techniques, multi -channel sound installations and network performances, creates sounds, tracks and atmospheres for film and television works. In cooperation with video artists he develops and presents conceptual mixed media projects. "Electronic media allows a playful intercourse with diverse techniques and styles. The feeling of alienation and transformation they produce are of interest to me, as is the application of acoustic ready mades and found objects within a musical framework" f.s. F.S. combines his sound generating equipment into a musical household of electronic instruments. Out of the European musical tradition, sound installations, music for unknown films and in applications for New Dance Culture or musique concrète he has created noise stories, songlines and dreamscapes in a very specific personal language. He has conceptualised numerous intermedia events, such as SWITCHBOX and THE LISTENING ROOM, in which his selection of sound arts, ambient music and improvised music, as well as elements from the electronic dance music scene are locked together in dense friction. works among others with David Moss, Jon Rose, David Shea, Yoshihide Otomo, Anna Homler, Thomas Heberer, Christian Marclay, Phil Minton, Sainkho Namtchilak, Sussan Deyhim, Dirk Raulf, Kalle Laar, Andres Bosshard performs since 1986 in various clubs, festivals and concert halls throughout Europe, for example: International New Jazz Festival Moers, Jazz Festival Leipzig, Jazz Festival Berlin, Festival International des Musiques Actuelles Nancy, GRAME Festival Lyon, ISEA 94 Helsinki, performances and projects on the documenta 8 and 9 in Kassel and on the XLV biennale in Venice Italy, Opera Leipzig and Dresden, Berliner Ensembel, IRCAM Paris, Musik Triennale Köln 1997, toured by order of the German Goethe Institut in Uruguay, Argentinia and Chile groups and projects switchbox - gameplay for 6 musical households Linguistic Research Laboratory - with David Shea and Yoshihide Otomo Timescales - by Chris Cuttler feat. composers.name: James Wyness
composers.bioText: I was born in Aberdeen, Scotland and now live in Jedburgh in the Scottish Borders. I studied French and linguistics at Aberdeen University and am about to begin a PhD in Composition. For many years my musical background was in performance, on conventional and more recently on hand-made microtonal instruments. My current interests are in electro-acoustic music, microtonality and contemporary choral music. At present I am exploring the idea of narrative, explicit and implicit, in acousmatic music. http://myweb.tiscali.co.uk/slowtones/ 1. chanson de geste [ listen ] 9'30'' 2. cut glass bowls [ listen ] 5'40'' 3. music to make you stop and start [ listen ] 9'57'' <home <back to guests // Last update:: October 30, 2013 //

composers.name: Matteo Milani
composers.bioText: Matteo Milani – 1974 - is a sound designer living in Milan. Actually he works in a post production facility, editing audio for cinema, tv and radio commercials. He started his career at the end of the 80’s in local radio stations, playing, editing and mixing music in “analogue” mode. He focused on dance projects, producing and applying electronic music on his dj activity, sequencing audio samples in his sessions. In the mid 90’s he pioneered the rising of digital audio workstations as Digidesign Pro Tools creative user. In the last years he studied and developed a deep interest in relationships between sound and picture. He joined Timet, reflecting most of his sensibility creating sound elements for new forms of art expression. Collaborations: - Game Programming Italia ( www.gameprog.it ), as a writer for interactive audio; - Symbolic Sound Corporation, home of the Kyma sound design language ( www.symbolicsound.com ), as a third party samples supplier. “…from the beginning of my creative process, like recording a real sound source, the same source suggests to me what is could became: I have discovered that, from my way of interpreting sound design, the best way to treat sound is to start from a ‘living” source, that remind us something familiar. Even though I am not a musician, I have always loved experimenting to build sound textures usign both noise and music elements, trying to fill the gap between these two worlds…”. You may find samples of his work visiting graphicalsound 1. random suite [ listen ] 6'36'' <home <back to guests // Last update:: October 30, 2013 //

composers.name: Purusha
composers.bioText: Purusha is born in 1999 from Emanuele Rodolà and is currently supported and complemented by the work of Luca Balsanelli and Valentina Gualtieri on the instrumental and vocal side respectively. Further collaborations with other artists are not sporadic and also extend the spectrum of sonorities and composing techniques he is interested in. Up until now he has released different works for labels such as Eerik Inpuj Sound, Hydrogen Dukebox, Saag Records and Ogredung, which he is the founder and runner of. Purusha analyzes sound and develops romantic and abstract unions. www.ogredung.org/purusha 1. fireworks (euneun) [ listen ] 4'29'' 1. nonant [ listen ] 3'08'' <home <back to guests // Last update:: October 30, 2013 //
